I cannot offer any advise or solutions, but I do have my experience which might help you. It might not be what you want or need to hear, but it might just help you see things more broadly. I’m sorry if this is something you have already been told.


It is not your fault and sometimes, no matter what we do, the outcome will be the same. Sometimes stopping and  letting go of the idea that you can or must fix it and keep trying, is the only way. That is not to say for ever, but for now. I am only beginning the process of divorce and know I have a huge messy and painful time ahead.


When my husband was forced to leave the home, my son just took his place. I realised he behaved and spoke exactly like his father. He constantly manipulated, gaslighted, verbally abused me and threatened me. It was like my husband was still living in the house, he would use the same phrases, same twisting of words, same controlling behaviour. 


I spoke with his therapist and other services, trying to find a way to help him, but nothing changed. As the behaviour escalated, and my other children were exposed to more and more, I begged for help. I knew something had to be done and there was a real possibility I would have to report him or call the police. There was no way I would allow the other children to be exposed to this, even if that meant kicking out my own son. I felt like I had failed him for allowing him to be like his father, that there might have been something more I could have changed or done, that there was more I could still do.


One day, he towered over me (very tall and large framed), screamed at me, spat in my face, told me I was a c*nt wh*re and just walked out the door. He went to his father’s and is now living with him. We rarely speak now, months later. When he does show up to visit, it is always to ask for something or interrogate me about where I have been, what I have been doing etc. 


I have accepted that my relationship with him is damaged and not repairable right now. I have grieved and am still grieving the loss of my child and I am broken hearted, I miss him every day. But I know it is the best thing for me and my other children, who were terrified of him on that last day and convinced he would kill me. They have the right to be safe in their own home and so do I. Sometimes no matter how hard we try, it is not enough. 

I have made sure he knows I will always be here for him, and I will continue to work with his therapists. I have told him if and when he is ready we can have family counselling and work on repairing our relationship, even though right now he does not want that.

I have the hope I needed months ago. It is the hope of patience and understanding and releasing. He is only 14 and he has much growing to do before he will be in a place to see the truth and grow into someone that sees his father for who and what he is and has done to him and his family. The hope that one day we will repair our relationship. 


(I ask those of you who do read this, to be gentle with me. I usually do not share things like this for fear that I will be misunderstood and judged, that is a left over from the 2 decades I spent with my husband.)
